findings.message: If the Postgres sidecar never passes its startup probe, the kubelet restarts it forever because of `restartPolicy: Always`. The agent init container then never starts, so the entrypoint never writes `$STATUS/exit` and never moves the work item to failed. The run only ends when `activeDeadlineSeconds` expires, and nothing in the pod says that Postgres was the cause. Possible failures include a non-Debian image under uid 1000 or a bad digest. Fix: bound the failure so it becomes visible. For example, document and test that the dispatcher or status reports a Job stuck in Init with a postgres reason, or have doctor validate `postgres_image` before dispatch.

Native sidecars (an init container with `restartPolicy: Always`) need Kubernetes 1.29 or later, or 1.28 with the SidecarContainers gate enabled. On an older K3s the field is dropped or rejected. A dropped field makes postgres an ordinary init container that never exits, so the agent never runs. Nothing in the diff checks the cluster version before rendering the sidecar. Fix: have doctor or dispatch refuse `postgres_image` when the server version is below 1.29, and state the requirement in the README Postgres bullet.
